en: The *Buddhabhāṣita-nitya-gaurī-viṣa-strī-dhāraṇī-mantra-sūtra* with its Ritual Procedures, translated by the Tripiṭaka Master Guputa.
Thus have I heard. At one time, the Buddha was staying at Śrāvastī in the Jeta Grove, the Garden of Anāthapiṇḍada.
He was together with a great assembly of one thousand two hundred and fifty bhikṣus,
as well as gods, nāgas, yakṣas, gandharvas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, mahoragas, humans, non-humans, and others, gathered for a communal discourse on the Dharma.
Universally opening the gate of dhāraṇī for all sentient beings,
he contemplates the Tathāgata and all sentient beings in the future evil age.
The three calamities arise in competition;
various evil venomous snakes and poisonous dragons move about, exhaling poisonous vapors,
while flying insects with poison kill and harm sentient beings.
Vipers, snakes, vipers, scorpions, centipedes, and their like; pythons,
venomous snakes, and all manner of evil, poisonous creatures—
whether they dwell in mountains or marshes.
Or they may be at the bottom of pits or in water,
all capable of releasing poison to afflict and penetrate sentient beings.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the great assembly, saying:
At one time, while I was on Mount Gandhamādana to the north of the Snowy Mountains,
I saw a young girl within those mountains,
her body adorned with the marks and signs of a hundred merits.
They wear deer skins as clothing and take various venomous snakes as their necklaces;
they play and associate with pythons, vipers, scorpions, and all manner of poisonous insects.
Hungry, I ate poisonous fruit;
thirsty, I drank poisonous gruel.
That woman saw me and acted as my companion.
"O Benevolent One, you must listen.
My constant *Gaurī* dharma-gate is able to extinguish all poisons in the world.
He then spoke the mantra, saying:

*Tadyathā:* *irimide* *tirimide* *iridi* *rimide* *namme* *nammarie* *nacce* *naccarie* *cakrāṇa* *vakrāṇa* *kaśmire* *kaśmirā* *mukite* *akṣiṇi* *akṣaṇi* *akṣagaṇi* *irīye* *akṣaye* *akṣape* *śvete* *śvetadundubhe* *anane* *loke* *svāhā*. At that time, the goddess Cāṅgulī, having spoken this mantra, [departed].
Within that Snowy Mountain there were five thousand venomous and evil dragons and snakes;
upon hearing the sound of this mantra,
they all fainted and their heads were simultaneously shattered.
The scales were scattered in all directions;
the fangs of the venomous snake fell out;
and the scalp was strewn like stars.
Blood flowed profusely from their wounds,
and they were all bound by their own fetters, unable to move or stop.
At that time, the World-Honored One observed these sentient beings who had been afflicted by the poison of the incantation.
He then spoke a heart-mantra to neutralize the aforementioned poison.
The mantra is as follows:

*Tadyathā | iri miri orami ri kṣakulu kṣakulu orami mi kuta ye kuta ye te suputa ye te suputa ye te namre nakaga khalanti re ekha visake tata tata sitata sitata sitata svāhā*. At that time, the World-Honored One, having spoken this mantra, [concluded].
All venomous dragons, vipers, and scorpions shall be restored to life and flee in all directions; their poisons shall no longer prevail.
Therefore, I now tell you, O son... [text missing].
You should maintain this "Constant Gaurī Poison Woman" mantra;
do not recite it in a loud voice,
but chant it before dragons and snakes.
Upon hearing this, the dragons and snakes will surely die.
The Buddha addressed the fourfold assembly:
"O sons of good family!"
If one seeks to save the world from the poisons of sentient beings,
at that time the mantra of the youth deity Cāṅguli can cure them all;
although this Cāṅguli manifests in a female body.
She is not actually a woman. Good son,
the wisdom and supernatural powers of the Buddhas and Bodhisattvas can manifest various bodies for the sake of sentient beings.
It gathers and transforms all poisons,
preventing malevolent venomous dragons and snakes from infesting and surrounding sentient beings.
If a person hears this Great Radiant Body Mantra of Cāṅguli, [they shall be protected].
"Seven years hence, you shall not be harmed by poison,
and you will also be able to destroy the poisonous evils within your own body.
At that time, the World-Honored One again addressed the King of Birds, Vainateya.
"You and your like-minded retinues, with your great strength and powerful hosts, must,
after my parinirvāṇa during the period of the Final Dharma,
likewise gather and subdue the various poisons; you must summon all ninety thousand of the *kroñca* birds and the *śuka* bird-kings, and you must completely uproot the ten thousand *māra*s."
"Upon hearing this Great Bright Mantra of My Constant *Gaurī*,
all must comply with it, provide support, employ skillful means, and offer protection, never acting in opposition. At that time,
the Buddha addressed the fourfold assembly.
"Good son, this mantra of the body of the poison-girl Nityagaurī can cure all ten thousand kinds of poisons in the world:

the venom of snakes, scorpions, and centipedes; malignant sores, carbuncles, abscesses, and smallpox; mountain and river poisons; the poison of raw gold; various medicinal poisons; and all manner of sorcery."
Simply consecrate water for drinking and for rinsing the mouth;
if it is for consecrating poison, recite the mantra three times,
repeating each [verse] seven times.
All poisons arise from their own root;
they cannot cause harm.
If one suffers from the poison of mountain streams, [this shall protect them].
If one washes the body with consecrated water and drinks the consecrated water,
all poisons from mountain streams will be completely eliminated.
If one can sincerely make offerings, pay respect, and uphold this divine mantra, [the same shall occur].
One shall obtain immeasurable merit.
At that time, the World-Honored One addressed the fourfold assembly:
"If there are sons of good family who are able to practice rescue and protection..."
One must paint the form of Cāṅgūlī as a young girl,
her body adorned with the marks and signs of a hundred blessings,
and wearing skin as her garment.
Clad in garments of *kauseya*,
with a great deity’s wheel-shaped topknot,
he holds in his right hand a sword that subdues poison.
In his left hand he holds the seal of the Poisonous Tree;
his entire body is adorned with necklaces, snake-braided bracelets, and armlets.
In front of the poisonous snakes, one should paint a youth dressed in green.
Place the water bowls, the incense altar, the hundred kinds of poisonous cakes,
and the various poisonous potions all before Cāṇḍālī;
draw mountains on each of the four sides surrounding her.
On both sides of the mountain, draw tigers, wolves, lions, vipers, poisonous dragons, scorpions, and various other venomous snakes surrounding it on all four sides.
If one constructs an altar,
its size may be one or two cubits according to one's intention.
Place an image upon the altar and recite mantras as an offering.
For the altar, use cow dung mixed with fragrant mud.
Having finished the offering of five plates of food and bird-head soup beneath the mud-puddle,
discard them in a clean place. Burn *mandārava* flowers as an incense offering and recite the mantra seven thousand times.
For superior practice, thirty thousand recitations;
for middling practice, seventy thousand recitations.
This can save the world and subdue poisons.
Simply consecrate water with mantras and have the patient drink it to cure all poisons.
Herein are the essential points of the Dharma taught in brief:

[For the mudrā, use a square piece of *lei-lei* (thunderbolt) jujube wood measuring one inch and seven fen; use vermilion to seal the poison and also seal it upon paper, which the patient shall swallow—this is highly efficacious for curing all illnesses].
[For the seal, use white sandalwood one inch and three fen [in length]; likewise for the preceding seal-paper, the seal-poison □, and the swallowing].
Banner. Banner-form image.
Shi shi shi shi. Flower tree flower tree. Sword-altar.
Banners. At that time,
when the World-Honored One had finished speaking this mantra,
there were immeasurable mantra-masters, yakṣas, asuras, garuḍas, kiṃnaras, humans, non-humans, and others within the assembly.
Having heard the Buddha’s teaching on the divine mantra for subduing poison,
they were all greatly rejoiced;
having fully approved it, they received and upheld it with reverence, prostrated, and departed.
This talisman is written with ink upon poison while reciting the mantra seven times;
it is highly efficacious. [Mantra: KUKU, KUKU, KUKU; JIJJ, JIJJ, JIJJ, JIJJ, JIJJ.
The *nitya-gaurī-ādhitiṣṭhana-mudrā*. Nitya-gaurī-lī. It cures all poisons.
Kou, kou-kou. Ri-ri-ri. Ri-ri-ri. Ri-ri-ri.
*Sā-ba* (Kill and bind), *Kin-ba* (Prohibit and bind), *Ten-shō* (Heavenly capture), *Sō-ka* (Lock and release).
Ri-ri-ri. Ri-ri-ri. Ri-ri-ri. Ri-ri-ri. [Write this with vermilion on paper, seal it, and wear it; it will eliminate all demonic influences.]
The talismans above should be written on paper with vermilion ink and ingested;
this will eliminate all ailments and pains within the abdomen.
One must treat them with great reverence and not defile them by touching them.
Regarding the mantra-deity,
some say that the second joint of the left ring finger is the "Eye of the Good," while the second joint of the right ring finger is the "Eye of the Evil Thief."
It further states:
"The middle joint of the left thumb is joined with the second joint of the ring finger; this is called the 'eye of the ghost,' and so forth.
Whenever a practitioner of recitation enters or exits, or comes into contact with any place, [they should perform this mudrā].
The *Yingyong chuhu tuoluoni* (Dhāraṇī for Protecting through Application).
Oṃ mūla-krodha hūṃ jaḥ. This was transcribed on the third day of the eighth month of the second year of the Renping era at Kuanshu Temple.
